justification: The pre-commit TSC error-count gate ran tsc even when frontend-nextjs/node_modules was absent (a bare git worktree). Without dependencies tsc cannot resolve types, inflating the count (~682) past the 677 baseline and false-failing the gate on commits that touch no TypeScript at all — forcing --no-verify repeatedly. There are zero real TS errors (verified non-incremental in a full checkout). Fix: skip the count when node_modules is absent; still enforce it in normal checkouts; the Vercel build type-checks on deploy as backstop.

break_it.scenario: A real new TypeScript error is introduced and committed from a bare worktree where the gate now skips
break_it.what_happens: the bad type would not be caught at commit time in that worktree
break_it.repro: introduce a type error in a worktree with no node_modules and commit
break_it.how: the gate still runs fully in any normal checkout (node_modules present), and the Vercel build type-checks on deploy and fails on a real error; the skipped context previously produced only a meaningless inflated count, never real enforcement

break_it.scenario: node_modules exists but is partial or corrupt, still inflating the tsc count
break_it.repro: delete part of node_modules then commit
break_it.how: out of scope for this fix and a different (broken dev env) failure; the directory-presence check covers the common bare-worktree cause; a corrupt install is a reinstall problem, not a gate problem

post_merge.secrets: None - no secrets or env vars touched.
post_merge.other_repo: N/A - hook change only. Git hooks apply after 'git config core.hooksPath .githooks' per clone/worktree, which existing clones already have.
post_merge.manual_verify: In a bare worktree (no frontend-nextjs/node_modules) a commit now prints 'Type check skipped' and proceeds; in a normal checkout with node_modules the gate still runs and blocks when the count exceeds 677. Confirm a deliberately added type error blocks a commit in the normal checkout.
